articles.title: Roku's Newly Released 65" 4K OLED TV Drops to a Bargain Price of $799.99 for October Prime Day
articles.summary: OLED TVs are considered the best TVs for gaming. They're usually quite expensive, but Amazon is offering a fantastic deal on a Roku branded OLED TV during the October Prime Day Sale. For two days only, the 65" Roku Pro 4K OLED TV is available for $799.99 with free shipping.
body: The Roku Pro-series OLED TV was released. It's equipped with a 4K true W-OLED panel with a native 120Hz refresh rate and HDMI 2.1 inputs, making it an excellent TV for PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X console gaming. Although the Roku Pro isn't as expensive as other OLED TVs, it shares most of the advantages of its more expensive siblings, including the near instaneous response time, true black levels, near infinite contrast ratio, and ultra-wide viewing angles. It also has one nice feature that the rest don't have, and that's the Roku smart interface baked in.

I've tried every built-in smart interface extensively, and I consider Roku to be the best smart interface overall compared to other popular options like Google TV (Sony), Tizen (Samsung), WebOS (LG), or Fire TV (Panasonic). The Roku interface is easy to use, aesthetically pleasing, light on resources, and most importantly for me, it doesn't require you to commit to an ecosystem. Roku also has native compatibility with just about every streaming app out there.
points: OLED TVs are considered the best TVs for gaming.
They're usually quite expensive, but Amazon is offering a fantastic deal on a Roku branded OLED TV during the October Prime Day Sale.

articles.title: BBC Reveals New Doctor Who Spinoff Starring a 'Young Doctor' With Blue Hair and a Robot Toaster Sidekick
articles.summary: Doctor Who may be on hiatus, but the BBC has just unveiled a new spinoff series for younger viewers: Doctor Who: TARDIS Crew. This animated series will feature a "young" version of the Doctor who is shown in official artwork to sport blue spiky hair.
body: Today's reveal for the series includes a confirmation of the production company behind the show, the London-based Alphablocks and Numberblocks creator Blue Zoo Animation Studio, and a projected launch in late 2027 or early 2028 — around a year before the BBC is aiming to bring the main Doctor Who back to U.K. TV screens.

"Created for CBeebies viewers, the series follows the Doctor, a young Time Lord, and his friends Hannah, Beastie and Toast-IE as they embark on extraordinary adventures through time and space," reads a blurb for the show. "Travelling aboard the iconic TARDIS, they encounter incredible creatures, discover amazing new worlds and come face-to-face with legendary Doctor Who foes, including the Daleks."

While this isn't the first we've heard of a new Doctor Who spinoff for younger viewers, this is the first time we've seen anything of its characters or aesthetic. The BBC has now also commissioned 52 episodes, each 11 minutes in length, with "preschool-friendly stories."

articles.title: Call Of Duty’s Richtofen Actor Wants Him To Come Back, Says 2027’s CoD Could Be From Sledgehammer
articles.summary: Veteran video game actor Nolan North has addressed his future in the Call of Duty series, saying he hopes to reprise his character Dr. Edward Richtofen from Black Ops' popular Zombies mode. If this does happen, it probably won't be soon.
body: Speaking at Gamergy in Puerto Rico ( via DomTheBomb ), North said he hopes Richtofen's story continues in a future Black Ops game, whenever that might be.

"I always like when they leave things open for the next one. I know that Infinity Ward and I think Sledgehammer has the next two before there is another Black Ops. I just don't want it to be the end of Richtofen, and I don't think it is," he said.

North clarified that he does not know for sure that Richotfen's story will continue, so he hoped people wouldn't think he had some inside knowledge apart from his own hope and belief. Whatever the case, North said Richotofen is one of his favorite characters to voice, and he hopes to reprise him someday.

North first appeared as Richtofen in 2008's World at War, and has reprised the role many times over in subsequent games from developer Treyarch. He's a fan-favorite character in the fan-favorite Zombies mode, with the story taking numerous twists and turns over the years.

articles.title: Solo Horror Dev Makes A Creepy Connection To A Real Haunted Island In Mexico
articles.summary: Being a haunted doll must be difficult. You're missing an eyeball, and your lipstick makes you look more like a cannibal than a cherub. People make faces of disgust at you in the antique mall, and you want to tell them you're actually the unblemished soul of a 19th century nun named Eunice, but…
body: The dolls of Mexico's Isla de las Muñecas, the Island of the Dolls, have been through a lot over the past 80 years. Folklore suggests the bald dolls cobwebbed and nailed to the island's trees contain the spirit of a drowned little girl, who caretaker Don Julian Santana may or may not have made up. In any case, he spent much of his life fishing plastic Barbies and babies out of the water near his home to honor her spirit. So Where Dolls Hang, which was featured in the Horror Game Awards' recent showcase this past summer, is a tribute, too--it honors the fact that our real world is often freakier than fiction.

"Some of the doll models you'll find were created using real photographs," developer Steelkrill explains on Twitter. "The photographs can also be found around in the game." An accompanying clip of first-person gameplay footage demonstrates with an image of a doll head coated completely in dirt and little pimples from raindrops. The Where Dolls Hang player then drops the photo and stares ahead; the same pimply doll head is sticking from a pike right in front of them.

articles.title: GameStop Is Preparing Us For Next-Gen Pricing With $1,400 Used PS5 Pros
articles.summary: Sticker shock might be underselling it with GameStop's new used pricing for Sony's most powerful system. Starting today, the video game store is listing pre-owned PS5 Pros for $1,400, though GameStop Pro members only need to dish out $1,330.
body: A generous take on GameStop's new strategy for used PS5 Pros is that the company's conditioning us ahead of the possibility that the PS6 could cost $1,000 or more. Obviously, Sony isn't the only one increasing hardware pricing and consoles probably aren't getting cheaper anytime soon --mainly because of the ongoing chip shortage from AI development.

A more cynical take is that GameStop is taking advantage of the situation similar to what scalpers do with the launch of new video game consoles. I'm also curious how many people now trade in a PS5 Pro at GameStop when they see how much the company is then reselling it for. Wouldn't an easier option just be to undercut them on Facebook Marketplace or eBay by $100?

Similar pricing for used PS5 Pro systems can be seen on Amazon and Best Buy's storefronts. One key difference here is that those are third-party sellers, such as this RYTEK example at Best Buy. GameStop is officially behind the pre-owned pricing on its own website.
points: Sticker shock might be underselling it with GameStop's new used pricing for Sony's most powerful system.

articles.title: 'Nier: Automata's 2B Officially Returns in Release Available Today
articles.summary: Square Enix is lending out the cast of Nier: Automata for another crossover. This time, three members of the acclaimed RPG's cast are coming to asymmetric multiplayer survival horror game Dead by Daylight. If that sounds exciting, then good news, the collaboration is available as of today, Oct. 6.
body: Beyond the amazing characters and incredible visuals, there's a definite connection between the themes of our two universes, both dealing with cycles of violence and suffering. Bringing 2B, A2, and Emil into The Fog gave us a chance to help celebrate what makes Nier: Automata so special to us.”

Unlike previous collaborations, the characters will be reskins of existing characters rather than completely new additions. On the Survivors' side, Feng Min is getting a 2B skin and Yui Kimura is getting an A2 skin. Both will be Legendary Outfits that come with unique music, voice lines, HUD icons, menu idle animations, and more. As for the Killer side, The Legion is getting a Very Rare Outfit inspired by Emil. This will also sort of make it feel like Nier creator Yoko Taro is personally hunting you down, so that's fun. The collection also includes an appearance by Pod 042 and Legendary portraits of 2B and A2.

articles.title: Warhammer Survivors Is Launching Mere Days Before GTA 6, And I Respect The Audacity
articles.summary: The next Survivors-like game--or Survivaton, as Vampire Survivors developer Poncle refers to them--is out soon, and it's threatening to cut into GTA 6 playtime. Warhammer Survivors launches November 10 on PC, consoles, and mobile devices, and you can also grab a new demo on PC via Steam right now.
body: Set in the grim (and dark) 41st millennium of the Warhammer 40,000 franchise, Warhammer Survivors sticks to the Vampire Survivors playbook: You'll fight all manner of Tyranid enemies that threaten the Imperium of Man, evolve your weapons, and die a lot before you're strong enough to start easily tanking the waves of heretical creatures. Extremis bosses will push your builds to the limit, and when it launches, the game will feature over 40 playable characters and an arsenal of 70 weapons to collect.

Warhammer Survivors will release on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Switch 2, and Switch next month, and it'll also be available via Xbox Game Pass. The new demo will give you a fresh taste of the carnage, featuring the heroes Lyssa Revenya and the Legend of Catachan.

It's one of the few November games willing to take a risk and launch close to November 19, as many publishers and developers have opted to avoid the GTA 6-sized elephant in the room. Only a few games are standing their ground, including one that features the king of the monsters, Godzilla.

articles.title: Say Goodbye to a Major Streaming Service With Paramount Plus Phaseout
articles.summary: HBO Max and Paramount Plus are two of the leading players in streaming, but the two will soon officially become one thanks to the recently completed merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery.
body: Paramount CEO David Ellison originally announced the plan to merge HBO Max and Paramount Plus back in March, before the merger under Skydance had been completed.

In a news release announcing the completion of the Paramount-WBD merger, Skydance promised that consumers "can expect greater innovation from a company built with technology at its core, including significant improvements to its direct-to-consumer streaming products, which will unify into a single service over time."

Skydance hasn't announced exactly how HBO Max and Paramount Plus will be unified, or what the name of the new streaming service will be. In a news release, the parent company simply refers to the streaming side of its business as "Skydance DTC." There's a good chance that Skydance or Skydance Plus will serve as the new name, with hubs dedicated to HBO Max, Paramount Plus, Discovery, and other brands.

articles.title: Someone's modded Diablo 2 for VR, and seeing the world through your character's eyes brings a whole new dimension to the series
articles.summary: Of all the games I thought I'd see converted to virtual reality, the Diablo games weren't among them, for some reason. But one industrious modder has set about changing that, converting probably the most well-liked Diablo game, Diablo 2.
body: Footage of the Diablo 2 VR mod was shared on Reddit and it shows the game being played in first-person, as the Sorceress explores the dingy starting area fields of the game, fireballing zombies and other enemies that are shambling nearby. It seems to work pretty well, with the player's left forearm showing the character's health and mana pools, and toolbar, and the inventory on their belt and map in their hand.

The Diablo 2 VR mod is made by Sergious - Reddit username Fantastic-Author2736 - and the mod files are made available on Github, should you wish to try it. Sergious made the mod with FlatVR and BodyWalk, but you don't need BodyWalk, apparently, to play it.

It's strikingly atmospheric seeing Diablo's world this way, through the character's eyes. The world is usually so far below you, as you look over it like a god from above, from an isometric vantage point. Not for the first time, it's made me wonder what Diablo would be like played from a much closer, over-the-shoulder camera angle, or even a first-person one. I'd half-expected Diablo 5 - recently announced at BlizzCon - to go this way, though it doesn't appear to be.

articles.title: All active Escape From Tarkov codes and rewards
articles.summary: Escape From Tarkov promo codes are used in the classic extraction shooter for all sorts of rewards. From in-game gear and weapons to currency, cosmetics, and more, redeeming as many of these Tarkov codes as you can will set you up for your next raid.
body: Here are all the currently active Escape From Tarkov promo codes, the rewards they grant, and how to redeem them in-game.

There are two ways to redeem promo codes in Escape From Tarkov. The first is to boot up the game launcher, then click on the drop-down arrow beneath your username in the top right-hand corner. Then select activate code and type in any of the codes listed above. If successful, you'll see green text telling you the reward has been claimed.

Alternatively, you can visit the official Escape From Tarkov promo code page on the website and type in the code there. Make sure you're signed in when you do so, and if you play Tarkov through Steam, ensure your account is linked.

When redeemed, go in-game and click on the messenger tab at the bottom of the screen. You'll find your rewards for each code by selecting "get" on all the messages. If you don't have the stash space for all of it, don't fret: you can come back and retrieve the rest of the rewards later on.

articles.title: "Keep it family friendly" - Sega's official Sonic Discord swarmed by 50,000 people in six hours, as understandably strict moderation is put in place
articles.summary: Sega has invited chaos upon itself by launching an official Sonic the Hedgehog Discord channel. Unsurprisingly, it's proven immediately popular, and strictly locked down. There is no fan art channel as of writing.
body: The announcement, made on official Sega social media accounts, reads as follows: "Looking for a place to chill and chat all things Sonic the Hedgehog? Maybe find people to race in Sonic Racing: CrossWorlds? We are excited to welcome you to the official Sonic Discord server!"

This post, made on X late last night, invited hordes of Sonic fans into the hub all at once, where there are various channels for discussion of Sonic games, movies, and comics. There's even an off-topic channel, which seems potentially unwise, and when Eurogamer explored the Discord server today, strict moderation features were in place.

For example, the server is currently on slow mode, meaning the quantity of posts made in each channel has been drastically reduced. There are also chat limitations in place, preventing newcomers to the server from posting at all unless they use a Discord Nitro boost (a paid service). A plea to "keep it family friendly" is present on the rules page as well.

articles.title: "Horrible day to be a Shion main" - Overwatch fans aren't happy about five new China-exclusive skins not coming to the rest of the world
articles.summary: Earlier this week, Blizzard released a new trailer for an upcoming event in Overwatch. Called 'Defiled Anthem', the event features skins and cosmetics for Shion, D.Mon, Kiriko, Reaper, and Emre, with the highlight of the whole activation culminating in a transforming 'Evolution' skin that changes…
body: Player sentiment, as you can imagine, has been negative: take a look at any Overwatch-focused subreddit or social media account, and you'll see the same complaints cropping up. But why does this happen? Why does Blizzard put out these skins in one region when it knows fans in another are going to complain?

Earlier this year, in an interview with IGN, Blizzard’s head of development for live games, Walter Kong, explained that the addition of Chinese-only skins is largely because of the studio's relationship with Chinese publisher Netease, which handles the promotion and management of the game in the region.

There's a pervasive feeling amongst international players of Overwatch that Chinese fans are 'treated better' than they perhaps are. In the past, players in the region would get free skins that were locked behind battle passes or needing buying in non-Chinese markets. In the past few days, these negative feelings have surfaced again; Reddit threads ask " what's the deal with [Overwatch] China?" whilst players on the dedicated Blizzard forums make accusations about 2023's Japanese character, Shion, being " supposedly claimed by NetEase ".

body: The stoves at Yuanyuan Manor still burn, and the simple warmth of everyday life rekindles old ties. A long-dormant stroke of ink is quietly bleeding into the breeze…

videos.title: DF Direct Weekly #284: Ghost of Yōtei QSSR Tested, Star Wars Galactic Racer, Gears E-Day PC
videos.summary: Thanks to Alienware for sponsoring DF Direct. To learn more about the Alienware AREA-51 Gaming Desktop, check out:
body: DF returns to QSSR coverage with a closer look at Ghost of Yōtei, with John weighing in with his opinions on Marvel's Wolverine too. Rich reveals that Sony isn't the first to port an AI upscaler to a non-AI based GPU, showing FSR 4 running on the RDNA 1 Radeon RX 5700 XT. Meanwhile, John's very happy with the PC version of Gears of War: E-Day. And after sharing some stories on anniversary DF content, the Star Wars Galactic Racer review embargo hits in real-time - and John's got a lot to say about it...
